title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 77-79). P is a set of 'points'. M is a set of 'pieces' X, each with a realisation |X| ⊂ P. Two pieces are disjoint, X ∥ A, when |X| ∩ |A| = ∅. For a family A ⊂ M:
- |A| is the union (or closed union) of the |X| for X in A.
- co-supp A = C_M(A) = {X ∈ M | X ∥ A} is the orthogonal of A.
- supp A = co-supp(co-supp A) is the bi-orthogonal closure.
- Σ_M is the set of closed families, the 'supports'. With the involution C_M, Σ_M is the complete ortholattice attached to the orthogonality (polarity) relation ∥.

The problem (pp. 77-79) is to compare this abstract 'lattice of supports' with the power set 𝔓(P) of the point set. On p. 77 Grothendieck has |C_M(A)| ⊂ P∖|A| and |A| ⊂ |supp A|, and he wants both to be equalities.

On this page he notes that the separation hypothesis of p. 77 is exactly the statement that the inclusion is an equality: |co-supp A| = P∖|A|. The hypothesis says: for x ∉ |A| there is a piece X disjoint from A with x ∈ |X|.

Applying the hypothesis twice gives |supp A| = P∖(P∖|A|) = |A|.

Lemma 2. Assume (iii_M), (vi_M) and the hypothesis. Then:
- |A| = |supp A| for every A.
- supp A ⊂ supp B ⟺ A ⊂ supp B ⟺ co-supp B ⊂ co-supp A ⟺ |A| ⊂ |B|. Lemma 1 had only one direction.
- Hence A ↦ |A| is an injective order embedding Σ_M → 𝔓(P) that commutes with the involutions C_M and C_P (complement). Compatibility with limits is queried.

Proof of the new direction. Suppose |A| ⊂ |B|. Then |co-supp B| = P∖|B| ⊂ P∖|A|. So each X ∈ co-supp B has |X| ∩ |A| = ∅, i.e. X ∈ co-supp A.

The next page goes on to ask whether finite and infinite meets/joins are preserved, i.e. whether |⋀A_i| = ∩|A_i|. That only goes through under the much stronger 'point-pieces' hypothesis: every singleton {x} is some |X|.
errors: Transcription '= A' after P∖(P∖|A|) must read '= |A|'. The margin formula should be |co-supp A| = P∖|A|, not P − A. Probably slips of the pen.

Tension, not resolved on the page. If pieces realise to open sets and |X| ∩ |A| = ∅ is read topologically (as p. 77 suggests, with closures), then the literal hypothesis forces every |A| to be clopen. In a genuine topological setting P∖|A| would have to be read as a pseudo-complement, e.g. the interior of the complement, as for regular open sets. Grothendieck's 'perplexités' on p. 77 point at exactly this.
The hypothesis is stated as equivalent to the union formula; that equivalence holds only if |·| of a family is a plain union, not a closure of a union. The notes switch between these conventions.

ideas.what: Orthogonality/disjointness relation on pieces, with 'support' as bi-orthogonal closure and 'co-support' as orthogonal; Σ_M is the ortholattice of closed families
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois connection; orthogonality spaces; closure lattice of a symmetric relation (formal concept analysis)
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs material is unpublished; the 'tame topology' theme appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism as far as I know

ideas.what: Separation hypothesis (every point outside |A| lies in a piece disjoint from A) is equivalent to |co-supp A| = P∖|A|; it implies Σ_M embeds in 𝔓(P) as an order embedding compatible with complements
ideas.modern_name: Representation of an ortholattice of closed sets in a power set; regularity-type separation axiom

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Galois-connection/orthogonality computation inside an exploratory axiomatics of 'pieces' for tame topology. The lemma is correct and elementary, and nothing here goes beyond standard lattice theory.
transcription_corrections: 'compl A' throughout is most likely 'co-supp A' (handwriting 'cosupp'; p. 79 writes |co-supp A| = P∖|A|).
The margin box reads |co-supp A| = P − |A| (the bars on A were dropped).
Under the union the index reads 'X ∈ M, X ∥ A', i.e. X ∈ co-supp A, rather than 'x ∈ M, x ∦ A'.
'Comme supp A = [-supp-] supp(compl A)' should read 'Comme supp A = co-supp(co-supp A)'.
Last line: 'commute aux involutions C_M, C_P'. The inserted note is probably '(com. limites ?)' or 'con. limites'; uncertain.
